title: Logical Contradiction
question_latex: Michelson-Morley found NO difference in light speed despite Earth moving at ${\sim}30$~km/s. Maxwell's equations predict $c = 1/\sqrt{\varepsilon_0\mu_0}$ as an absolute constant. Derive the simplest assumption that resolves this contradiction.
key_insight_latex: Simultaneity is not absolute; time itself is relative to the observer's motion.

title: Mathematical Derivation
question_latex: Lorentz showed length contracts by $\gamma = 1/\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}$ to preserve Maxwell's equations. Starting from the Lorentz transformation, derive the corresponding time transformation.
key_insight_latex: Time dilation: $t' = \gamma(t - vx/c^2)$.

title: Conceptual Synthesis
question_latex: A train passenger and platform observer both measure the same light beam at $c$, yet their clocks run at different rates. Identify the assumption about time that must be abandoned.
key_insight_latex: Relativity of simultaneity --- simultaneous in one frame is not in another.

title: Energy-Mass
question_latex: A body at rest emits two equal light pulses in opposite directions (total energy $L$). Analyse the body's mass before and after emission using energy and momentum conservation.
key_insight_latex: $E = mc^2$: mass and energy are equivalent.

title: Aether Elimination
question_latex: Every aether-detection experiment has failed. Using Occam's Razor, propose the most parsimonious hypothesis consistent with Maxwell's equations.
key_insight_latex: Postulate $c$ is constant for all inertial observers; discard the aether.

title: Velocity Addition
question_latex: A moves at 0.6$c$ relative to B, and B moves at 0.6$c$ relative to C. Newtonian addition gives 1.2$c > c$. Derive the correct relativistic formula.
key_insight_latex: $w = (u+v)/(1+uv/c^2)$ prevents superluminal speeds.

title: Equivalence Principle
question_latex: You are in a sealed box feeling a force into the floor. Describe two entirely different physical situations that would produce an identical experience.
key_insight_latex: Gravity and acceleration are locally indistinguishable --- the equivalence principle.

title: Gravitational Time Dilation
question_latex: An accelerating rocket's trailing clock runs slower than its leading clock. Using the equivalence principle, derive the corresponding gravitational effect.
key_insight_latex: Gravitational time dilation: $\Delta t_{\text{lower}} = \Delta t_{\text{upper}}\sqrt{1 - 2GM/rc^2}$.

title: Photoelectric Effect
question_latex: Light of frequency $f$ ejects electrons from a metal. Electron energy depends on $f$, not intensity. Explain this using the minimum number of new postulates.
key_insight_latex: Light consists of discrete quanta (photons) each with energy $E = hf$.

title: Wave-Particle Duality
question_latex: Electrons through a double slit produce an interference pattern, yet each electron arrives at a single point. Propose the simplest theoretical framework explaining both observations.
key_insight_latex: de Broglie: $\lambda = h/p$; matter has wave properties; probability amplitude determines detection.

title: Base Composition
question_latex: Chemical analysis shows [A]$\approx$[T] and [G]$\approx$[C] universally, ratio $\approx$1:1. What structural arrangement of the bases explains this universal constraint?
key_insight_latex: Complementary base pairing via hydrogen bonds: A pairs with T, G pairs with C.

title: X-ray Pattern
question_latex: X-ray diffraction of DNA shows: (1)~3.4~\AA{} reflection, (2)~${\sim}$34~\AA{} reflection, (3)~X-shaped helical cross, (4)~${\sim}$20~\AA{} diameter. Propose the 3D structure consistent with all four.
key_insight_latex: Double helix: 3.4~\AA{} base stacking, 34~\AA{} per turn (10 bases/turn), ${\sim}$20~\AA{} diameter.

title: Backbone Chemistry
question_latex: DNA's phosphate backbone is negatively charged at physiological pH and readily accessible to solvent. Use this to determine which component is on the outside and which is inside the structure.
key_insight_latex: Phosphate backbone on OUTSIDE (solvent-accessible); bases point INWARD.

title: DNA Replication
question_latex: DNA has two complementary antiparallel strands. When it replicates, each daughter cell must receive an exact copy. Propose the replication mechanism and its prediction for isotope labelling.
key_insight_latex: Semi-conservative replication: each strand serves as template; confirmed by Meselson-Stahl.

title: Protein Secondary Structure
question_latex: Pauling showed the alpha-helix is stabilised by regular hydrogen bonds. Identify the specific N-H---O=C donor-acceptor geometry and the resulting geometry.
key_insight_latex: Alpha-helix: N-H of residue $i$ hydrogen-bonds to C=O of residue $i+4$; 3.6 residues per turn.

title: RNA Synthesis
question_latex: RNA polymerase synthesises RNA using a DNA template. State the direction it reads the template and the direction it synthesises RNA. Apply to template 3\mbox{'}$\to$ATCG$\to$5\mbox{'}.
key_insight_latex: RNA polymerase reads template 3\mbox{'}$\to$5\mbox{'}, synthesises RNA 5\mbox{'}$\to$3\mbox{'}; template ATCG gives mRNA UAGC.

title: Continental Drift
question_latex: Continents show mirror-image coastlines, matching fossils, and identical rocks across oceans. Wegener's mechanism of continents ploughing through oceanic crust is mechanically impossible. Propose a valid mechanism.
key_insight_latex: Seafloor spreading: new crust at ridges, subduction at trenches; mantle convection provides driving force.

title: Magnetic Anomaly
question_latex: Symmetric magnetic anomaly stripes are mapped on either side of mid-ocean ridges --- positive and negative alternating in mirror-image patterns. Explain their origin.
key_insight_latex: Seafloor spreading with periodic geomagnetic reversals recorded in solidifying basalt.

title: Seismic Evidence
question_latex: S-waves are blocked by a zone starting ${\sim}$2900~km deep. P-waves continue but refract at this boundary. Determine what material property causes this.
key_insight_latex: Liquid outer core (molten iron-nickel) blocks S-waves; solid inner core refracts P-waves.

title: Subduction Volcanism
question_latex: Volcanoes form above subduction zones even though the subducting slab is cold. Explain why subduction causes melting.
key_insight_latex: Water released from subducting slab lowers mantle melting point (flux melting); arc volcanism results.

title: Isostasy
question_latex: Mountain ranges have deep roots extending into the mantle; ocean basins are comparatively shallow. Using crustal and mantle densities, derive the relationship.
key_insight_latex: Isostasy (Airy): crust floats on denser mantle; root depth $\delta = h\,\rho_c/(\rho_m - \rho_c)$.

title: Strategic Interaction
question_latex: Two companies choose High or Low price independently. $\pi(H,H)=(10,10)$; $\pi(L,L)=(3,3)$; $\pi(H,L)=(1,12)$; $\pi(L,H)=(12,1)$. Find the stable equilibrium.
key_insight_latex: Nash equilibrium: both choose Low (dominant strategy); Prisoner's Dilemma.

title: Mechanism Design
question_latex: A government must allocate spectrum licences to highest-value companies. Companies know their own value but not others'. Design a mechanism where truth-telling is the optimal strategy.
key_insight_latex: Vickrey (second-price) auction: winner pays second-highest bid; truth-telling is dominant strategy.

title: Comparative Advantage
question_latex: Country A produces 1 car or 2 tonnes of wheat per worker-day. Country B produces 1 car or 3 tonnes. Show which country should specialise in which good and why trade benefits both.
key_insight_latex: Comparative advantage: A specialises in cars, B in wheat; both gain from trade.

title: Public Goods
question_latex: A lighthouse prevents shipwrecks for all passing ships. No ship can be excluded from its benefit; one ship using it does not reduce its value to others. Explain why private provision fails.
key_insight_latex: Public good (non-excludable, non-rival): free-rider problem causes market undersupply.

title: Information Asymmetry
question_latex: Used car sellers know quality; buyers do not. High-quality car owners want \$10,000; low-quality owners accept \$5,000. Buyers offer the expected value. What happens to the market?
key_insight_latex: Adverse selection (Akerlof's Lemons): high-quality cars exit; market collapses.

title: Information Coding
question_latex: DNA has 4 bases; proteins have 20 amino acids. A 1-base code gives only 4, a 2-base code 16. Determine the minimum code length and its prediction for synonymous mutations.
key_insight_latex: Triplet code: $4^3 = 64$ codons for 20 amino acids; degeneracy at codon position~3.

title: Regulation Logic
question_latex: Bacteria grow on glucose. Add lactose as sole carbon source: they initially struggle, then rapidly synthesise lactose-metabolising enzymes. Remove lactose: enzymes disappear. Propose the switching mechanism.
key_insight_latex: Operon model: repressor blocks transcription; lactose binds repressor, releasing block.

title: Enzyme Kinetics
question_latex: An enzyme catalyses E + S $\rightleftharpoons$ ES $\rightarrow$ E + P. At low [S], rate is linear; at high [S], rate plateaus. Derive the rate equation.
key_insight_latex: Michaelis-Menten: $v = V_{\max}[S]/(K_m+[S])$; saturation at $[S] \gg K_m$.

title: Membrane Transport
question_latex: Cell membranes are selectively permeable: water and gases cross freely but Na$^+$ and K$^+$ do not. Explain the structural basis and how ions are nonetheless transported.
key_insight_latex: Hydrophobic lipid bilayer blocks ions; protein channels (passive) and pumps (active/ATP) provide selective transport.

title: Gene Regulation
question_latex: Liver cells and neurons contain identical DNA but express entirely different protein sets. Explain how cells with identical genomes produce radically different phenotypes.
key_insight_latex: Transcription factors bind promoter sequences; epigenetic marks (methylation, histone modification) stably maintain cell-type identity.

title: CMB Prediction
question_latex: If the universe began in a hot dense state, it should produce a radiation afterglow as it expanded and cooled. Predict the current temperature and spectrum.
key_insight_latex: CMB: ${\sim}2.7$~K blackbody (microwave spectrum), redshifted from ${\sim}3000$~K at recombination ($z \approx 1100$).

title: Galaxy Rotation
question_latex: Galaxies show flat rotation curves: outer stars orbit at nearly the same speed as inner stars, contradicting Keplerian $v \propto 1/\sqrt{r}$. Propose the simplest explanation.
key_insight_latex: Dark matter halo: non-luminous gravitating mass ($\rho \propto 1/r^2$) extends beyond visible disk.

title: Stellar Nucleosynthesis
question_latex: Stars fuse hydrogen to helium, releasing energy. Iron has the highest binding energy per nucleon. Explain how elements heavier than iron form.
key_insight_latex: Elements heavier than iron forged in core-collapse supernovae via rapid neutron capture (r-process).

title: Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram
question_latex: When stellar luminosity is plotted against surface temperature, most stars fall on a diagonal band. Explain the physical origin of this main sequence.
key_insight_latex: Main sequence: stars in hydrostatic equilibrium burning hydrogen; $L \propto M^4$.

title: Hubble Expansion
question_latex: Galaxies show redshifts proportional to distance: more distant galaxies recede faster. Does this imply the Milky Way is at the centre? Explain what is actually expanding.
key_insight_latex: Hubble's law $v = H_0 d$; no centre --- every galaxy sees others receding; space itself expands.

title: G\"{o}del Incompleteness
question_latex: G\"{o}del showed any consistent formal system powerful enough for arithmetic contains true unprovable statements. What does this imply for Hilbert's programme to formalise all of mathematics?
key_insight_latex: Hilbert's programme is impossible; truth $\neq$ provability; mathematics cannot be fully mechanised.

title: Computability
question_latex: Can an algorithm determine, for any mathematical statement, whether it is provable in finite time? Prove your answer using diagonalisation.
key_insight_latex: Halting problem: assume universal decider, derive contradiction via self-reference; no such algorithm exists.

title: Cantor Diagonalisation
question_latex: Assume all real numbers in $[0,1]$ can be listed: $r_1, r_2, r_3, \ldots$ Construct a real number $d$ not in the list and explain the implication.
key_insight_latex: Cantor diagonalisation: $d$ differs from $r_n$ at digit $n$; reals are uncountable.

title: G\"{o}del Numbering
question_latex: G\"{o}del's proof requires formal statements about arithmetic to refer to other formal statements. Describe the encoding scheme that makes this self-reference possible.
key_insight_latex: G\"{o}del numbering: assign unique integers to symbols, formulas, and proofs via prime factorisation; arithmetic becomes self-referential.

title: Second Incompleteness
question_latex: G\"{o}del's second theorem addresses whether a formal system can prove its own consistency. State the result and its implication for Hilbert's consistency programme.
key_insight_latex: A consistent system $S$ cannot prove $\text{Con}(S)$; Hilbert's consistency programme is unachievable.
